en.title: Amazon OA #116: Make a Good String
en.description: You are given a string s containing only 0 and 1. A string is called good if it contains neither the subsequence "010" nor the subsequence "101" (subsequences need not be contiguous). Each operation changes one 0 to 1 or one 1 to 0. Find the minimum number of operations needed to turn s into a good string.
en.input: One line with a 01 string s. 1≤(length of s)≤10^6.
en.output: Output one integer, the minimum number of operations.
en.explanation:
Example 1: s="111101110100"; changing the 0s at positions 5 and 9 (1-indexed) to 1 gives "111111111100", 2 operations in total.
Example 2: "01010" can become "00000" or "01111", among others, needing at least 2 operations.
Example 3: "1100" is already good, so the answer is 0.
hints: Containing neither subsequence means the characters switch at most once.
A good string can only have the form 0…01…1 or 1…10…0.
Enumerate the split point and use prefix counts to compute the number of flips.
